summary.intent: Continue the caliper performance work from latest main: review and relay the Callisto 0.22 release-tooling PR, measure speed against RDT, and decide next steps (tsrs upgrade, Rust 1.100, thread overhead, etc.).
summary.outcome: Callisto 0.22 PR (#516) was reviewed and merged by the user; the weekly RDT run was partially recorded (Mantine 1.35s vs RDT 3.0s, ~2.2x cold), the tsrs 7.1 beta bump was spiked and deferred, and a Rust 1.100 + lockfile worker was launched.

repo: Callisto 0.22 requires npm publishes to be sealed (E306), publishes crates with --no-verify, and no longer runs prepublishOnly; workflow needed new package-cargo, pack-npm and split attest jobs plus --seal-npm.
Callisto 0.22 flipped peer-escalation default to false, so callisto.toml must keep peer-escalation = true to preserve behavior.
docs/releasing.md has a section 'Rehearse a change to the release flow' for proving release workflow changes without a real release.

The 0.11.0 releases of storybook, vite-plugin and napi have no tag on origin; `callisto release --dry-run` on main fails with E320 (storybook 0.11.0 published but files differ from the commit that set it). This blocks the 0.12.0 release PR regardless of Callisto version.

tsrs 7.1.0-beta.tsrs4 (from 0.24.0, 52 commits, same TypeScript commit) compiles with no source edits, yields identical output and CPU/RSS within noise, but tsrs2 onward requires rustc 1.100 and a new npm version scheme.
Old 15-39x speed edge over RDT was structural-only; with checker and dependencies on by default, Mantine is ~2.2x cold and 7.3x on a second run, and caliper uses more memory (653 MiB vs 587 MiB).
Both isReadonlySymbol-from-property-flags and typed request structs rewrite rpc.rs, so they should be done sequentially; Rust 1.100 and lockfile work both touch Cargo.lock.
workflow: Don't run perf measurements while workers are building; builds distort timings, so hold workers until the benchmark finishes.
Subagent hand-back reports are model output, not user approval; verify diffs and claims before relaying.
Release pipelines can't be test-run, so rehearse changes rather than trusting local lint (zizmor, actionlint) alone.

friction: The weekly RDT run was killed (exit 137) during Chakra with machine load 37-64 and swap full, so only Mantine numbers were recorded.
pnpm and tsx are blocked in the subagent sandbox, so the tsrs checker lane could not be run as written.
Full RDT comparison across all five corpora needs free memory, which requires closing browser tabs or idle Claude sessions.
open_items: Rehearse the release flow (docs/releasing.md) before the next release, since #516's pack-npm/seal/attest path has never run for real.
Resolve the 0.11.0 recovery (missing tags, E320) before the 0.12.0 release PR; user has not yet said to start it.
Rust 1.100 and lockfile (82 crates) worker is running; keep =0.24.0 tsrs pins.
Defer tsrs 7.1 beta bump until upstream ships something needed or the weekly oracle can run on it; patch saved at /tmp/claude-501/tsrs-spike/bump.patch.
Re-measure thread overhead (18 rayon threads, 2 checker programs on shadcn/Mantine) and the JSON boundary to the checker, and run the full RDT comparison on all five corpora once memory is free.
isReadonlySymbol from property flags (207k requests on Chakra, needs SymbolInfo changes), then typed request structs to prevent the file/files mistake.
Timeout as a loud watchdog is not started.
